title: MZ Pixel Art Tiles Jitter and Blur During Movement

posts.author: vandrac123
posts.body:
I am facing a fairly complex issue in my project. The entire game uses pixel art, from the tiles and menus to the bitmap font itself. At first, I had problems with the native blur in RPG Maker MZ, but I managed to work around it by using the Pixel Perfect plugin.
After that, another obstacle came up related to the camera framing, since RPG Maker displays a very large portion of the map by default. I was able to solve this with some zoom plugins, but I ended up noticing an even more serious issue. Whenever the character walks or runs, the tiles slightly jitter, and while running this effect becomes more pronounced, with a noticeable blur appearing as well.
I have already disabled all plugins and confirmed that this is a native engine issue. When using the default tiles, this effect is present but almost imperceptible. However, when working with pixel art graphics, the problem becomes extremely noticeable and significantly harms the game’s visuals.
I have looked into many plugins, both paid and free, but none of them solved the issue. I am not an experienced programmer, and I have been stuck for quite some time, unable to move forward with the project because of this problem. That is why I am reaching out here in search of help to finally overcome this obstacle.

posts.body: You will need to code some kind of pixel perfect camera.

posts.author: FleshToDust
posts.body: Instead of zooming in, what if you played the game at a lower resolution? The lower the resolution, the fewer tiles you see on the screen.

posts.author: vandrac123
posts.body:
FleshToDust said:
Instead of zooming in, what if you played the game at a lower resolution? The lower the resolution, the fewer tiles you see on the screen.
Click to expand...
It’s a good suggestion. The zoom code was so stable that I honestly never even considered this. I’ll definitely test it. However, the issue with tiles shaking and blurring during movement is kind of a problem that already comes with MZ itself — even with the default tiles and no additional code, it’s already noticeable. When you use pixel art sprites, it becomes even more apparent.
I’ve researched that even in more flexible engines like GameMaker and Godot, additional camera configurations are sometimes necessary for pixel art to look consistent. I believe it will be necessary to rewrite MZ’s camera to use a Perfect Pixel Camera, as Archeia suggested. I had hoped that a plugin to fix this already existed, but it seems that there isn’t one…
